review_comments: Why don't you use a spinlock instead? It already has all the asyncness you're looking for.

The current code was already using a SemaphoreSlim (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/21558/files#diff-a751368b99293f26ab0b48c583add848L36), I didn't want to change the semantics of it. Just wanted to make sure we timed out
I don't think we do this elsewhere in the codebase, could we avoid it here to keep consistency with the rest of the codebase?
Is there a way we can avoid introducing this class? I don't get what value it adds other than throwing an exception. Couldn't we encapsulate that into a helper method instead?
How strongly do you feel about this? Seems like more work to undo what is perfectly reasonable code.

I want to avoid adding complexity where we don't need it on this code. I want to keep this code as simple and concise as possible. Otherwise it becomes unmanageable. The important thing here is the name and we can probably just need a method for it (unless I'm missing something).

We've been careless in this area before just adding stuff for "fixes" and it ends up causing trouble, so I want to keep things as simple as possible. I don't feel strongly about it, so I'll leave it up to you, but my preference is that we keep things as lean as possible.
